archetype.name: Point Guard (Payton quick game)
archetype.definition: A distributor who lives on screens and short, horizontal throws inside Sean Payton's timing system, winning with volume, protection and red-zone execution rather than arm-driven chunk plays, with mobility that has gone quiet this year.

report.headline: Screens and stalled third downs are hiding a passer still near his baseline
report.take:
Nix has been a specific kind of quarterback for two years. His efficiency was above average (0.089 and 0.105 EPA per play, 25th and 23rd), but his yards per attempt never were (6.66 and 6.42, 40th both years). He covered that with volume, an aDOT around 7.4-7.5, and real rushing value: 430 and 356 yards. The 2026 version keeps the low-YPA shape and has lost most of the extras. His -0.016 EPA per dropback ranks 26th, his 6.07 YPA ranks 35th, and he has 25 rushing yards in four games.

The biggest driver is scheme. Thirty-seven of his 135 attempts, about 27%, have been thrown behind the line, and those plays are running at -0.235 EPA with a 32% success rate. Every throw past the line has been positive: 0.12 EPA short, 0.102 intermediate, 0.197 deep. His intended air yards have fallen to 6.21, and his throws land 2.76 yards short of the sticks on average. Week 4 at San Francisco was the extreme case, with 2.4% aggressiveness and 4.6 intended air yards on 42 attempts. That diet costs him most on third down, where he faces 6.9 yards to go, converts 30%, and posts -0.394 EPA. Courtland Sutton has taken 22 targets at -0.519 EPA per target, which makes things worse.

The raw numbers also hide the schedule. All four opponents rank in the top half of defenses today (9th, 7th, 4th and 14th). The opener at Kansas City in 91-degree heat, with four sacks, a lost fumble and -14.4 passing EPA, accounts for more than the whole season's deficit. Weeks 2-4 combined for +12.0 passing EPA. The protection is real: Denver allows the 2nd-lowest QB hit rate, and his 3.6% sack rate ranks 7th. What isn't propping him up is the five red-zone touchdowns on 20 attempts. That scoring has kept his fantasy line respectable, at 14.3 PPR per game, and it is the piece most likely to cool.

From here, efficiency should drift back toward his career band as the schedule softens, because protection and positive EPA past the line are stable traits. The ceiling depends on two things Denver controls: fewer throws behind the line and more designed runs. Those designed runs have been good (0.305 EPA on 7 plays). Losing Pat Bryant (0.95 EPA per target, doubtful and expected to miss a few weeks) takes away the receiver who has turned his throws into the most value.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, few sacks
strengths.body: Denver's line allows the 2nd-lowest QB hit rate in the league. Nix has been pressured on just 16.4% of dropbacks and sacked on 3.6%, 7th-best. Four of his five sacks came in the Week 1 heat at Kansas City, so this looks structural rather than lucky, and it matches his 2025 pressure-to-sack rate of 17.2% (8th).

strengths.title: Positive at every depth downfield
strengths.body: Once the ball crosses the line he is productive: 0.12 EPA short, 0.102 intermediate and 0.197 deep. The deep and intermediate samples are small (11 and 20 attempts), but the pattern says the passer is fine. The distribution of throws is what's failing.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: All five of his touchdown passes came inside the 20, with 0.324 EPA per play and positive CPOE there. Payton's red-zone design is a real asset. Still, five scores on 20 attempts is a rate that should come down even if he stays good there.

concerns.title: Too many throws behind the line
concerns.body: More than a quarter of his attempts are screens and swings that lose value (-0.235 EPA), and his average throw lands short of the sticks. This is a play-calling choice more than a Nix flaw, but his intended air yards (6.21) sit below his career aDOT of 7.4-7.5, so the offense has gotten more horizontal. Unless Denver dials it back, it caps his YPA and efficiency.

concerns.title: Third downs are stalling
concerns.body: He converts 30% on third down, with -0.394 EPA and -9.5 CPOE, and the average distance is a manageable 6.9 yards. The cause is partly the throwing-short-of-the-sticks habit and partly Sutton's poor efficiency. Third-down rates are noisy over 40 plays, but this is where the season's EPA deficit is concentrated.

concerns.title: The rushing value has vanished
concerns.body: After 430 and 356 rushing yards in his first two seasons, he has 25 on 14 carries. He has scrambled only three times (2.1% of dropbacks). The dossier lists no injury, so the cause may be clean pockets or a coaching choice. Either way, it removes a floor that used to cover for his low YPA.

trend.note: Passing EPA swung from -14.4 at Kansas City to +8.4, -1.1 and +4.7, and PPR output went 5.4, 14.1, 24.1, 13.6. The last three weeks are steadier and net positive, but Week 4's ultra-conservative 2.4% aggressiveness shows how much the game plan, not Nix, sets his range.

nextGame.headline: Strong Chargers rush, broken Chargers offense: a low-scoring script likely
nextGame.body:
The Chargers' pass rush is the real test. They rank 3rd in QB hit rate and 6th in sack rate, which runs directly into Denver's 2nd-ranked protection. Their coverage is more vulnerable: 25th in explosive pass rate allowed and 20th in deep EPA. Their offense is the bigger story. It ranks 31st in EPA, its line allows the league's highest QB hit rate, and it runs well above expectation (-9% pass rate over expected). That projects a slow, low-possession game in which Denver leads and Nix doesn't need volume. Against a QB-friendly 2 TDs per game allowed, this is a manageable but not juicy spot.

Availability tilts it Denver's way. Derwin James (94% of snaps) is out, and corner Donte Jackson is questionable, which weakens the deep and middle coverage Nix has barely tested. Dalvin Tomlinson's absence thins the interior. On the other side, Rashawn Slater is out 4-6 weeks, Kayode Awosika is out, and Joe Alt and Trevor Penning are questionable. That is a shredded line facing a Denver defense that ranks 6th in QB hit rate, which should mean short fields. Denver's own loss is meaningful: Pat Bryant is doubtful and expected to miss a few weeks. More targets will go to Sutton and RJ Harvey, who have been far less efficient.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers rush vs Denver protection
keyMatchups.body: LAC gets home on QBs at the 3rd-highest rate, and Denver allows the 2nd-fewest hits. Nix's pressure-to-sack rate of 21.7% is mid-pack, so if the rush wins, sacks follow. Watch whether the Tomlinson absence softens the interior push.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots without Derwin James
keyMatchups.body: LAC ranks 20th in deep EPA allowed and 25th in explosive pass rate, now without its starting safety. Nix has been positive deep but has only 11 such attempts. This is the one place the matchup offers upside if Payton opens the playbook.

keyMatchups.title: Short fields from LAC's line
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers' offense ranks 31st in EPA and its injury-riddled line allows the most QB hits, facing Denver's 6th-ranked hit rate. Turnovers and short fields would feed Nix's best area, the red zone. The counterweight is Denver's 31st-ranked run defense against a run-heavy opponent, which can drain the clock.

nextGame.watch: Whether Denver keeps living behind the line of scrimmage or finally attacks a James-less secondary downfield.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts that hold are protection, sack avoidance and positive EPA once the ball goes downfield. He has had those traits across three seasons, and four straight top-half defenses have depressed them. Expect his EPA per dropback to climb back toward the 0.05-0.10 range, with YPA stuck in the mid-6s as it has been his whole career. His CPOE of -2.93 should edge up toward his career range near zero. The red-zone touchdown rate will cool, so passing TDs settle around one and a half per game.

The swing is usage. If designed runs and scrambles return toward his first two seasons, his fantasy floor rises several points. If Denver stays this screen-heavy without Bryant, he looks like a low-ceiling game manager. With Bryant out for a few weeks, Sutton's efficiency has to rebound for the passing game to open up.
swingFactors: Share of throws behind the line
Return of his rushing and scrambling
Sutton's efficiency while Bryant is out

bets.reason: LAC's offense ranks 31st in EPA and 29th in pass EPA. Its line already allows the highest QB hit rate and is now missing Slater and Awosika, with Alt and Penning questionable, against a Denver defense 6th in hit rate. The risk is Denver's 31st-ranked run defense against a run-heavy Chargers attack.

Three of Denver's four games went under. LAC's offense is near the bottom of the league and passes 9% below expectation, which shortens games. Nix's 6.07 YPA and screen-heavy diet don't produce quick scores. LAC's 25th-ranked explosive pass defense is the main threat to the under.

confidence.note: Four games and 145 dropbacks against a tough schedule, but two seasons of stable career baseline to anchor against.
